clue.text: Girl I cast in Charlie Chaplin's original masterpiece

indicators.note: to be cast in a film is to be placed within it, so one group of letters is put inside another

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the original of something is where it starts, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the comedian's name
a lass is a girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is given a role in Charlie Chaplin's first great film.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Chaplin reads as one name, but the two words do separate jobs: Charlie is C, and Chaplin's original is another C, with LASS and I cast between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of lasting excellence, the kind of acknowledged great work also called a masterpiece.

clue.text: Copper fines hosts to stop supplying

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house, so one chunk is put inside another

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
F is the abbreviation for fine (as on pencil and pen grades), so two of them make the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer, a copper, issues fines that halt someone's supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman handing out fines; it is the metal's symbol. CU and FF join to make CUFF, which then hosts TO in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off a gas or water service is to stop providing it, so the phrasal verb matches the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Visiting Greece, maybe right to go later on

indicators.note: going later means moving further along the word, so a letter is lifted out and set back in nearer the end

parts.note: someone visiting Greece, for example, is overseas
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A traveller in Greece is told the right moment to leave will come later.
explanation.walkthrough: ABROAD is the word abroad; take its R out and put it back one place later, after the OA, and ABROAD becomes ABOARD. The single word on is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship, train or plane is being aboard it, so the preposition and the adverb share a meaning.

clue.text: Twisted American individual Italy caught speeding

indicators.note: something twisted round is turned the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: US is the standard short form for American
an individual is a person
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A crooked American is arrested in Italy for driving too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a speeding ticket; only the two letters for American are twisted, and the rest is a straight charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A supersonic aircraft travels faster than sound, so it is going at extreme velocity; the adjective fits a sense of speeding loosely.

clue.text: Shelter unlit by arc light occasionally erected

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means put up, so the letters read from the bottom upwards
taking the letters lightly and only now and then, every other one, from the words that follow 'Shelter'

parts.note: the even letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A shelter left in darkness except when an arc light flickers on now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arc light' looks like a single lamp, but the fodder stops at 'arc': 'light occasionally' takes N, I, B, A, C from 'unlit by arc', and 'erected' turns them upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small hut or simple dwelling that gives shelter.

clue.text: What Cows Chew, excellent filler for telly — turned over channel!

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
a filler goes into the middle, so these letters fill the telly abbreviation

parts.note: TV, the television, which telly is British slang for
cows chew the cud, food brought back up for chewing again
A1 means excellent, written with I for the figure 1

explanation.surface: A TV schedule fills airtime with a programme about cattle before someone switches channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' is not a TV station but the definition. Excellent is A1, written with I for the one; 'filler for' packs the cows' food and that into the telly abbreviation, and 'turned over' reads the result backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a raised structure carrying a road or railway, and like an aqueduct can serve as a channel for traffic or water.

clue.text: What actor may say, failing to hold Oscar up

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within your grasp, so one letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a failing is a moral weakness, a vice
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
when time is up, it is over

explanation.surface: An actor might say something after failing to win the Academy Award, the Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests the Academy Award; here it is just O. Up here means finished, as in time is up.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice-over is narration spoken by an unseen performer, so it is lines an actor delivers off screen.

clue.text: Supporter, 24, on a cycle

indicators.note: a cycle moves round in a loop, so the last letter loops back to the front

parts.note: the answer to clue 24, which is IDEA

explanation.surface: A sporting fan follows a cycle race, cheering a rider.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to the answer of 24 Down; 'on a cycle' moves its final A round to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant who helps and backs up a more senior person.

clue.text: Meal with no starter scored a hit

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so having none means losing the opening letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
to score a surface is to cut a line into it

explanation.surface: Someone skipped the first course of dinner and still scored a success.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter plays on the first course of a meal; here it is the first letter. Scored looks like goals or points but means incised.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a boxer's upward punch to the chin, so it is one kind of blow.

clue.text: Almost dropped winning ace for nothing — that's scruffy

indicators.note: one thing given for another is a swap, so a letter is replaced by a new one

parts.note: to totter is to wobble and nearly fall
O looks like zero, nothing
A is the abbreviation for ace, here pictured as a winning serve or card

explanation.surface: A player nearly collapsed but served an ace to win, though they look a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the O of TOTTERED for an A. Winning is surface colour for the ace; it gives no letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered clothes are torn and ragged, which makes their wearer look shabby and unkempt.

clue.text: Bad time to retire from company? On the contrary

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: poor means bad
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bad moment to leave a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the wordplay comes from the definition; On the contrary turns that round, so company comes from bad time retiring. It is a coda, not a mechanism, and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers or a band of people, and a company is likewise a body of troops or a group.

clue.text: Perhaps Venetian covers urn showing Achilles' heel

parts.note: Venetian blinds are one kind of window covering, hence perhaps
an urn is a pot

explanation.surface: A Venetian scene on a covered urn depicts the wounded heel of Achilles.
explanation.walkthrough: Covers looks like a container verb, but it is a noun: the window covers are BLINDS. Achilles was invulnerable except at his heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind spot is an area of weakness or ignorance, just as an Achilles' heel is a single vulnerable point.

clue.text: One doesn't follow warning from driver who speeds?

parts.note: fore is the shout a golfer gives on hitting a ball, often off the tee with the club called a driver
a runner is one who speeds along

explanation.surface: A motorist who speeds gets a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist, but it is the golf club; the shout 'fore!' warns people ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner is a predecessor or herald, one who goes ahead rather than coming behind.

clue.text: Cockney trio at liberty

indicators.note: a Cockney accent says th as f, so the word is spelt as it is pronounced in that London speech

parts.note: a trio is three of something, which a Cockney pronounces with an f

explanation.surface: Three East Londoners have been let out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, in which th is said as f.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at liberty is not imprisoned or confined, and the adjective means exactly that.

clue.text: Fun broadcast delayed, getting fixed

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
lagging behind means delayed

explanation.surface: An entertainment programme went out late and was rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast suggests a TV show; it scatters the three letters of fun. Fixed here means steady, not rigged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unflagging effort never weakens or tires, so it stays constant and steady, a loose sense of fixed.

clue.text: After spliff, suggest partnership

parts.note: a spliff is a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint
to venture an opinion is to put it forward

explanation.surface: After smoking a spliff, someone proposes going into business together.
explanation.walkthrough: Spliff is slang for a cannabis cigarette; joint is the commoner word.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint venture is a business arrangement in which two firms share an enterprise, a kind of partnership.

clue.text: Fruit aren't nice liquidised

indicators.note: liquidising pulps food in a blender, so these letters are mashed into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Some fruits taste unpleasant once they have been blended into a smoothie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the fruit and the blender together, which is apt: liquidised does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Irishman wound up server, downing one drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, winding something up raises it, so the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name in crosswords

indicators.note: to down an opponent is to knock them out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a waiter serves at table
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An annoyed Irishman taunted a waiter while knocking back a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing pretends to mean drinking, but it knocks the I out of WAITER. Wound up suggests annoyed; in a down entry it turns PAT upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap water is water from the mains supply, something people drink.

clue.text: It has grated cheese inside cool topping

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, signalling that one chunk sits within another
inside says where the second chunk goes: within the first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: grating breaks food into shreds, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be shredded

explanation.surface: A dish, a cool topping, contains grated cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a recipe; the grated cheese is shuffled and put between the two letters of It.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice sheet is a vast layer of frozen water covering land, a cold covering lying over the ground.

clue.text: Bit of a ring round about backing city contracting in far north

parts.note: an arc is a section of a circle or ring

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the shortened city word is reversed
contracting means shortening, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the word city
the last letter of city
a circle is something round, going all about

explanation.surface: A piece of a ring road runs round a shrinking city in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracting' cuts the Y from 'city' to give CIT, which 'backing' turns to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic Circle is the line of latitude near 66.5 degrees north marking the polar region.

clue.text: Number revealed in the first two digits

parts.words: Number revealed in the first two digits
parts.note: surface reading: a figure found inside the opening digits of something longer; setter's reading: write down the first digit and then the second, side by side, and read the result as a number

explanation.surface: A number is hidden in the opening pair of digits of some longer figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Revealed in suggests a hidden word, but no letters are hidden. Put the digits 1 and 2 next to each other and the number they show is 12.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve is a whole number, the one written with the digits one and two.

clue.text: Perfect example of a Spoonerism: "Wherefore, Robin?"

indicators.note: of a Spoonerism says the quoted phrase is to be spoken with its opening sounds swapped, as Reverend Spooner was said to

parts.note: wherefore is an old word for why
a robin is a bird

explanation.surface: A quotation in the style of Shakespeare asks a robin why.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Why, bird?' aloud and, as 'of a Spoonerism' asks, swap the opening sounds W and B: it becomes 'by word'.
explanation.definitionFit: A byword is a person or thing cited as the perfect example of some quality.

clue.text: Sponge possibly used to be hard

parts.note: was is the past of be
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A sponge that was once soft has gone hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Sponge is a verb here, not the bath item or the cake; possibly says it is one way of doing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge a surface is to clean it with a damp sponge, one example of washing.

clue.text: Secretaries approach fencing master in hall

indicators.note: a fence surrounds an area, so one chunk is enclosed by another

parts.note: PAs are personal assistants
an approach is a way of doing something
a sage is a wise master

explanation.surface: Office secretaries walk up to a fencing instructor in a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Fencing master reads as a swordsmanship teacher; fencing is the container verb, and a sage is a master of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall in the sense of a corridor or entrance passage is a passageway through a building.

clue.text: George V lost, upholding "What you should do"

indicators.note: the first half of 'upholding': in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
the second half of 'upholding': the words hold the answer's letters inside them, running across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run on across George V lost

explanation.surface: A history note that King George V suffered a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upholding' does two jobs: holding hides EVLOS inside 'George V lost', and up reverses it. The definition refers to what the solver should do with this very clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A solver's job with any crossword clue is to work it out, so this is a self-referential definition.

clue.text: Clue I would answer with electronic input

indicators.note: input is something put in, so one letter is placed inside the rest

parts.note: I'd contracts I would
A is the abbreviation for answer
e- is short for electronic, as in email

explanation.surface: Someone would answer a crossword clue by typing it in electronically.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue sounds like a crossword clue but is the definition, as in I haven't a clue. E goes in between ID and A.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase not have a clue, clue means notion, so a clue in that sense is an idea.

clue.text: Routine theatre ad — millions taking it in

indicators.note: taking it in means the answer is held within the words that precede it

parts.note: the letters run on across theatre ad millions

explanation.surface: A theatre advertisement brought in millions of viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking it in' signals the answer lies within the words before it: the end of 'theatre', all of 'ad' and the start of 'millions'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a figure for a monotonous, unending routine of work.

clue.text: Defaced big and small room in above-18 residence

indicators.note: defaced means its face, its first letter, is removed

parts.note: the word big
the first letter of big
loo is a British word for a toilet, the smallest room in the house

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a large house and its tiny room in an adults-only residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defaced' strips the B from 'big', leaving IG. '18' points to the answer of 18 Across, the Arctic Circle; a home found above it is in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome-shaped snow house, a dwelling of the Arctic.

clue.text: Sign with the Gunners to provide competition

parts.note: the Royal Artillery are called the Gunners
a trace is a sign or mark left behind

explanation.surface: A footballer signs for Arsenal to challenge for a place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal, a London football club, and sign suggests a transfer; here the Gunners are the Royal Artillery, RA, and sign is TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce struggle for success in working life, a cut-throat contest.

clue.text: One may calculate, for example, gallons needed by van

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
G is the abbreviation for gallons
the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: Someone works out how many gallons of fuel a van needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Van suggests a vehicle; it is the vanguard, the head. The definition reads loosely: an intellectual is someone who might do sums.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is a bookish intellectual, the sort of clever person who does mental arithmetic.
